paragraphs.en: Play cards to change a shared total and make opponents lose tokens. Everyone starts with nine. You are eliminated when you cannot pay a penalty; the last player left wins.
Two to eight players receive three cards each. A round starts at zero. On your turn, read the total with C, browse your hand with the arrows and play a card with Enter.
The card changes the total. If the round continues, you receive a replacement and play passes to the next person.
Cards affect the total as follows:
- A 3 through 8 adds its face value. Playing a 7 at 20 makes 27. A 4 also reverses play when at least three players remain.
- Queens and kings add 10.
- A jack adds 10 and skips the next player. With two players, you play again.
- A 9 leaves the total unchanged.
- An ace adds either 1 or 11. After playing it, choose with the arrows and Enter.
- A 10 adds or subtracts 10. Subtraction is available when the total is at least 10; choose with the arrows and Enter.
- A 2 doubles the total, except that it halves an even total above 49. At 40 it makes 80; at 60 it makes 30. The current total determines its effect, so there is no choice to make.
Watch the thresholds of 33 and 66 when raising the total:
- Land exactly on 33 or 66 and every opponent loses one token. From 32, for example, play an ace as 1 to charge everyone else.
- Cross a threshold and you lose one token for each threshold crossed. Raising 30 to 35 crosses 33 and costs you one.
Reaching or passing 99 ends the round:
- Exactly 99 costs every opponent two tokens.
- Exceeding 99 costs you two tokens. If the same play also crosses 66, it costs three in total.

The next round starts at zero with fresh hands. S reads tokens. Zero tokens does not itself eliminate you: you leave only when the next penalty exceeds what you can pay. With one token, paying one leaves you in the game, while a penalty of two eliminates you.
Before play, the host can change these settings:
- Starting tokens may be higher or lower. Elimination still works the same way.
- Omniscient bots know everyone's cards. Without the option, they do not have that advantage.
- A turn timer penalises timeout with the loss of one token and the turn. Your hand and the shared total stay unchanged.
Arrows: browse cards.
Enter: play a card or choose an ace or 10's effect.
Escape: cancel a value choice without playing.
H: read your hand.
C: read the shared total.
S: read everyone's tokens.
Z: find the next legal card; a card needing a value choice is only selected.
Shift+Z: find the previous legal card; a card needing a value choice is only selected.
T: read whose turn it is.
Shift+C: sort by suit; repeat to reverse.
Shift+H: sort by rank; repeat to reverse.
Shift+M: restore received order.
